Chi-square test of homogeneity of two categorical samples

Source: R/drift.R
drfthomog.Rd

Tests whether two samples of a categorical variable (offence type, region, race in last year's and this year's release) were drawn from the same distribution, by Pearson's chi-square on the 2-by-k table of their counts.

Usage

drfthomog(x, y, seed = 1L)

Arguments

x, y

Factors or text (or named count vectors): the reference and the new sample.

seed

The seed of the Monte Carlo branch, one whole number from -2147483647 to 2147483647.

Value

A named numeric vector of class drfthomog: statistic, df, p_value and logpvalue, with the attribute method and the inputs in the attribute lakner.

Details

With pooled shares \(\hat\pi_j = (x_j + y_j)/(n_x + n_y)\), $$X^2 = \sum_j \frac{(x_j - n_x\hat\pi_j)^2}{n_x\hat\pi_j} + \frac{(y_j - n_y\hat\pi_j)^2}{n_y\hat\pi_j}$$ on \(k - 1\) degrees of freedom. Three branches, named in the attribute method: "chi-square approximation" when every expected count is at least 5; "Monte Carlo permutation (small expected counts)" otherwise, the p-value from stats::chisq.test() with simulate.p.value = TRUE and B = 10000 tables with the same margins, drawn under seed with the caller's random stream restored (p_value is then at least 1/(B+1)); and "inapplicable: ..." for a single category or fewer than two observations per category, where no test has power and p_value is NA rather than 1.

drftchisq() takes the reference as known; when it is itself a finite sample, that ignores its sampling error and reports drift too readily. This test estimates the shared distribution from the pooled margins and carries the uncertainty of both samples, the right test for two releases of a table. Categories present in only one sample are given zero counts in the other.

See also

drftchisq(), stats::chisq.test().

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- sample(c("x", "y", "z"), 300, TRUE)
b <- sample(c("x", "y", "z"), 300, TRUE)
drfthomog(a, b)
#> drfthomog: statistic =  0.5150, df =  2.0000, p_value =  0.7730, logpvalue = -0.2575 
#> inputs: nx = 300, ny = 300, k = 3 
#> method: chi-square approximation 
drfthomog(a, sample(c("x", "y", "z"), 300, TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1)))
#> drfthomog: statistic =  6.978e+01, df =  2.000e+00, p_value =  7.030e-16, logpvalue = -3.489e+01 
#> inputs: nx = 300, ny = 300, k = 3 
#> method: chi-square approximation 
drfthomog(c(a = 30, b = 20), c(a = 25, b = 25))
#> drfthomog: statistic =  1.0101, df =  1.0000, p_value =  0.3149, logpvalue = -1.1556 
#> inputs: nx = 50, ny = 50, k = 2 
#> method: chi-square approximation 
attr(drfthomog(c(a = 3, b = 1, c = 2), c(a = 1, b = 4, c = 1)), "method")
#> [1] "Monte Carlo permutation (small expected counts)"
try(drfthomog(c(1, 2), c(a = 3)))
#> Error : drfthomog: a numeric `x` must be named.
